pairs: Onus verbi Domini ad Israël in manu Malachiæ.
The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi.
“In what way have you loved us?”
Was not Esau brother to Jacob,
And have I not loved Jacob,
et posui montes ejus in solitudinem,
And I have set his mountains in solitude,
et hæreditatem ejus in dracones deserti.
and his inheritance with the serpents of the desert.
Quod si dixerit Idumæa: Destructi sumus,
But if Idumea will say, “We have been destroyed,
sed revertentes ædificabimus quæ destructa sunt:
but when we return, we will build up what has been destroyed,”
thus says the Lord of hosts:
And they will be called “The limits of impiety,” and,
et populus cui iratus est Dominus usque in æternum.
“The people with whom the Lord has been angry, even to eternity.”
“May the Lord be magnified beyond the limits of Israel.”
says the Lord of hosts to you,
o sacerdotes, qui despicitis nomen meum,
who despise my name. And you have said,
Offertis super altare meum panem pollutum,
You offer polluted bread upon my altar, and you say,
in eo quod dicitis: Mensa Domini despecta est.
In that you say, “The table of the Lord has been despised.”
If you offer the blind for sacrifice,
et si offeratis claudum et languidum,
And if you offer the lame and the sick,
if he will be pleased with it,
or if he will accept your face,
Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei ut misereatur vestri (de manu enim vestra factum est hoc),
And now, beseech the face of God, so that he may have mercy on you (for by your hand has this been done) if,
in any way, he might accept your faces,
Quis est in vobis qui claudat ostia,
Who is there among you that would close the doors
and enflame my altar without pay?
non est mihi voluntas in vobis,
I have no favor in you,
et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra.
And I will not accept a gift from your hand.
Ab ortu enim solis usque ad occasum,
For, from the rising of the sun even to its setting,
magnum est nomen meum in gentibus,
my name is great among the Gentiles,
et in omni loco sacrificatur: et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda,
and in every place, a clean oblation is being sacrificed and offered to my name.
quia magnum est nomen meum in gentibus,
For my name is great among the Gentiles,
Et vos polluistis illud in eo quod dicitis:
And you have polluted it, in that you say,
“The table of the Lord has been contaminated;
and that which is placed upon it is contemptible,
compared with the fire that devours it.”
and you have exhaled it away,
And you brought in by plunder the lame,
and brought it in as a gift.
numquid suscipiam illud de manu vestra?
How can I receive this from your hand,
Maledictus dolosus qui habet in grege suo masculum,
Cursed is the deceitful, who holds in his flock a male, and,
et votum faciens immolat debile Domino: quia rex magnus ego,
when making a vow, offers in sacrifice that which is feeble to the Lord.
For I am a great King, says the Lord of hosts,
et nomen meum horribile in gentibus.
and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles.
